---
title: "Troubleshooting"
---

*Reference: [CLI](cli.qmd) · [Front matter](frontmatter.qmd) · [Cell options](cell-options.qmd) · [Configuration](configuration.qmd) · [Shortcodes](shortcodes.qmd) · Troubleshooting*

The preview surfaces most problems as a small **diagnostics** note in the corner
(non-fatal) or a dismissible **error overlay** (a failed render). Here are the
common ones.

## Code cells show as source / "kernel unavailable"

There is no Jupyter kernel. Set `QMD_FAST_PYTHON` to a Python that has
`ipykernel` (and `QMD_FAST_R` for R with `IRkernel`):

```sh
pip install ipykernel
export QMD_FAST_PYTHON="$(which python3)"
```

The diagnostics note usually quotes the kernel's own error (e.g. *"No module
named ipykernel"*), so fix that and save: the server respawns the kernel and
re-runs automatically, no restart needed.

## A cell hangs / runs forever

A cell that exceeds `QMD_FAST_CELL_TIMEOUT` seconds (default 120) is interrupted
(SIGINT → `KeyboardInterrupt`); the warm kernel and prior cells survive. Lower it
for tighter feedback, or set `0` to disable the cap. The dev menu's **Restart
kernel** drops and respawns the kernel if it's truly wedged.

## A cell ran, but I think the kernel crashed

If a kernel process dies mid-session (a segfault in a native library, an
out-of-memory kill), qmd-fast self-heals rather than hanging. The cell that was
running when the kernel died gets a *"kernel exited before this cell ran; it will
re-run on the next save"* placeholder, and the **next** run notices the dead
process, drops it, respawns a fresh kernel, and re-runs every cell from the top
(the new kernel holds no state, so the warm prefix is gone). You don't have to
touch **Restart kernel** for this: a crash recovers on its own with the next save.

A failed *start* (a missing or misconfigured interpreter, not a mid-run crash) is
different: qmd-fast backs off for about 20 seconds before retrying, so a genuinely
broken `QMD_FAST_PYTHON`/`QMD_FAST_R` doesn't re-hang every save. During the
backoff the cells render as source with the "kernel unavailable" diagnostic. Fix
the interpreter and the next save within a few tries recovers on its own; or hit
**Restart kernel** to clear the backoff and try immediately.

## Outputs look stale, or I want to force a clean re-run

Cell outputs are cached in `_freeze/` (gitignored) keyed by a cumulative content
hash, so an unchanged cell (and everything upstream) restores from disk instead of
re-executing. The key folds in this cell's code, every same-language cell above it,
and the interpreter id, so a real edit always busts the cache: there are no stale
hits to clear by hand. Two escape hatches exist if you suspect the cache anyway:

- The dev menu's **Restart kernel** forces the next run to ignore disk-cache hits
  and re-execute every cell against a fresh kernel (then re-persist), so it doubles
  as a "re-run everything from scratch" button.
- `QMD_FAST_NO_CACHE` ignores the cache entirely and never writes it, so every run
  re-executes. Reach for it when comparing timings, when a cell has a hidden
  non-determinism you're debugging (a clock, a random seed, an external fetch), or
  to confirm a result reproduces from cold rather than from a replayed output:

  ```sh
  QMD_FAST_NO_CACHE=1 qmd-fast build report.qmd
  ```

  Note the cache is already correct by construction (errors and `#| cache: false`
  cells are never persisted), so this is a debugging tool, not a routine step.

## Diagrams / `{js}` cells don't render

Mermaid loads from a CDN, so it needs `http(s)` and a network. `{js}` cells run
offline (d3 + Plot are bundled), but a cell that `import()`s a relative helper module
needs `http(s)`, not `file://`. Use `preview` (or a deployed/served build). Prose,
math, and executed figures render offline regardless.

## "Port already in use"

`preview` automatically tries the next few ports and logs the substitution. Pass
an explicit port if you want a specific one: `qmd-fast preview file.qmd 5000`.

## A broken `{{< include >}}` or extension

A missing include leaves an HTML comment breadcrumb and a diagnostics note, so it
never fails silently.

## Edits aren't picked up

The watcher follows source/asset file types (`.qmd`, `.bib`, `.css`, images, …)
under the document's directory and any `{{< include >}}`d file's directory, and
skips build-output/VCS folders (`_site`, `_book`, `.git`). Editing a file outside
those won't trigger a refresh.

## A deck looks unstyled

A custom deck theme usually comes from a format extension
(`format: <ext>-revealjs`). Confirm the extension loaded (no warning in the dev
menu) and that its `_extensions/<ext>/` directory sits beside the `.qmd`.

## `--host` preview is refused from my phone (or shows "needs its session link")

`--host` gates non-loopback access behind a per-session token, so a request without
it gets a 403. Open the **exact** URL from the QR code or the printed `network`
line (it carries the `?t=…` token); a hand-typed `http://<ip>:<port>/` is refused
on purpose. The token is regenerated on every server start, so an old QR or a
bookmarked URL from a previous run stops working: rescan the current one. Browsing
from the same machine (`127.0.0.1`) never needs the token.

## The VS Code companion preview won't connect

The companion spawns a plain `qmd-fast preview <file> <port>` and points its webview
at `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/`. It binds **loopback only**: it does **not** pass
`--host`, so there is no LAN token to fumble and no firewall hop to clear. If the
panel stays blank:

- Make sure `qmd-fast` is on the path the extension uses. It runs whatever the
  `qmdFast.path` setting points at (default `qmd-fast`); set it to an absolute path
  if the editor's environment doesn't see your shell's `PATH`.
- The extension waits up to a few seconds for the server to answer on its port. If
  you see *"qmd-fast preview did not answer"*, the binary failed to start: run the
  same `qmd-fast preview <file>` in a terminal to read the real error.
- Because it's a loopback URL, do **not** add `--host` or a token: that's for phones
  on your LAN, not for the local webview.

## A large site previews or builds slowly

A first cold build of a site with many executed cells has to run them once; after
that, `_freeze/` does the heavy lifting. Things that keep it fast:

- **Let the freeze cache warm up.** The first run populates `_freeze/<page>.json`;
  every later `build`/`preview` of an unchanged page replays its outputs from disk
  and never boots a kernel. Don't delete `_freeze/` between builds (it's safe to
  commit if you want CI to skip execution), and don't set `QMD_FAST_NO_CACHE`, which
  defeats exactly this.
- **Use `--no-exec` for a structure-only pass.** When you're iterating on layout,
  navigation, or prose and don't need fresh cell outputs, render the code cells as
  source and skip the kernel entirely:

  ```sh
  qmd-fast preview ./site --no-exec
  ```

  The pages render in full (chrome, links, math, figures already in the cache stay
  put as source) at a fraction of the cost, which is also the right call when you
  just want to eyeball a big site's shape.
